cards.headline: Millions in Syria struggle to access safe water and sanitation, MSF reports

pages.text: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) stated on September 24, 2026, that millions of people in Syria continue to struggle to access safe water and sanitation following 14 years of conflict, displacement, and damage to essential infrastructure. MSF water and sanitation coordinator Charlie Hardstone warned that unreliable water supplies increase the risk of waterborne diseases and complicate healthcare delivery, noting that water appearing clean may contain harmful bacteria and contaminants. This situation affects people returning to communities where basic infrastructure remains damaged. According to the UN High Commissioner for Refugees, approximately 3.8 million Syrians displaced within the country or abroad have returned since December 2024. The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs estimates that 15.6 million people in Syria still require humanitarian assistance.

Flooding in northeastern Syria has placed additional pressure on water infrastructure. MSF reported that floods in May and August damaged dozens of water stations in Raqqa and Deir ez-Zor. In response, the organization rehabilitated several facilities, including the Al-Hari water station in Deir ez-Zor, which improved water access for approximately 11,000 people. In Hasakah, MSF supplied more than 3.5 million liters of water to displaced populations and donated a desalination plant with a daily production capacity of 800,000 liters of drinking water.

cards.headline: Bill Gates calls for government safeguards and monitoring of artificial intelligence

pages.text: On September 25, 2026, Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates called for government safeguards and the monitoring of artificial intelligence, warning that increasingly powerful AI tools could be used by individuals with malicious intent to cause catastrophic harm. During an interview with NBC News’ “Meet the Press,” Gates stated that AI is “certainly powerful enough to drive events” that could result in a billion deaths, arguing that the combination of advanced technology and people seeking to cause harm presents an unprecedented risk. He described the combination of people with ill intent using the latest AI tools as a weapon more powerful than anything previously seen. Gates urged politicians and law enforcement agencies to be involved in determining required safeguards and how AI systems should be monitored, noting that while such oversight would create “a little bit of overhead for the industry,” it should not dramatically slow AI development.

pages.text: According to MyJoyOnline, the White House has barred the broadcaster CNN from traveling with President Donald Trump on Air Force One for a trip to Tennessee scheduled for Saturday. CNN reported that no other outlet was listed as a replacement in the president's tentative schedule. On Saturday, Trump criticized CNN and other media outlets in a series of online posts, referring to them as 'fake news.' This development follows a September 24, 2026, incident where the White House denied entry to some CNN and MS NOW reporters assigned to cover arrivals for a state dinner for Chinese leader Xi Jinping.

cards.headline: Sylvester Mensah urges Latenu FM to promote trade and export opportunities in Ga

pages.text: Sylvester Adinam Mensah, the Chief Executive Officer of Ghana EXIM Bank, has proposed collaborating with Latenu FM, a community radio station in La, to provide information regarding business growth, trade, and export opportunities in the Ga language. Speaking as the Special Guest of Honour at the station's 10th anniversary celebration on Saturday, Mr. Mensah urged the station to utilize its platform to highlight local entrepreneurs and assist listeners in understanding available business and financing opportunities. He stated that the station should use its platform to celebrate local entrepreneurs, explain financing and trade opportunities, and inspire young people to create rather than only seek jobs. Mr. Mensah, a former MP for La Dadekotopon, expressed a willingness to explore how the station and institutions such as Ghana EXIM Bank could work together to make business information more accessible to local communities. He noted that the initiative could be extended beyond the Ga language to other Ghanaian languages to help disseminate national information to a wider audience. The anniversary ceremony included the presentation of awards to individuals recognized for their contributions to communities in La and the wider Ga traditional area.

cards.headline: Iran proposes seven-day plan to reopen Strait of Hormuz

pages.text: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated on September 25, 2026, that Tehran has conveyed a seven-day plan to Washington via Qatar to end hostilities and restore normal maritime passage through the Strait of Hormuz. According to Araghchi, the waterway would reopen on the seventh day if specific required conditions are met. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian noted that the ceasefire process could begin once Washington accepts the proposal, though Araghchi emphasized that Iran would not accept coercion or threats. The proposal reportedly includes a seven-day cessation of hostilities across the Middle East, including Lebanon, the release of at least $12 billion in frozen Iranian assets, an easing of U.S. sanctions on Iranian oil, and an end to the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports. This plan builds upon a memorandum of understanding reached between Washington and Tehran in June that aimed to end the conflict, reopen the strait, and restart nuclear program negotiations, though that agreement later collapsed. While The Wall Street Journal reported that U.S. President Donald Trump rejected the proposal, citing U.S. officials, Reuters reported that Iran was still awaiting an official U.S. response. The Strait of Hormuz has been central to a nearly seven-month U.S.-Iran conflict.

cards.headline: Syria reconstruction estimated to take decades as aid remains insufficient

pages.text: Tjada McKenna, chief executive of Prosper Global, stated that Syria faces a “multi-decade” recovery process due to widespread destruction of homes and essential infrastructure. Speaking in New York on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, McKenna told The National that international assistance reaching the country remains “woefully insufficient” relative to the scale of reconstruction required. The World Bank estimates Syria’s reconstruction needs at approximately $216 billion. While millions of Syrians remain displaced, there have been increasing returns following the fall of Bashar al-Assad in December 2024. McKenna, who traveled through Aleppo, Idlib, and Damascus several weeks prior to her remarks, identified the restoration of water and electricity networks, roads, hospitals, and schools as immediate priorities, alongside the creation of jobs and livelihoods for returning families.

McKenna warned that Syria’s recovery is occurring during a global funding crisis where humanitarian aid budgets are declining while needs increase across multiple conflict zones. She noted that the transition from emergency relief to economic recovery will take time due to the scale of reconstruction, competing crises, and reduced international aid. Prosper Global is currently providing emergency assistance to displaced Syrians while shifting toward long-term recovery efforts, such as supporting agriculture and restoring water infrastructure. McKenna also noted that the lifting of Western sanctions has raised hopes for increased foreign investment, which could potentially allow more companies and suppliers to operate within the country.

cards.headline: President Mahama denies plans to declare state of emergency over illegal mining

pages.text: President John Dramani Mahama has dismissed reports claiming he intends to declare a state of emergency to address illegal mining, known as galamsey. Speaking to Ghanaians in New York on September 25, 2026, Mahama stated he had never announced plans to invoke such a measure, asserting that a state of emergency should only be considered as a last resort. He noted that while such measures can address serious national challenges, they are generally intended to be temporary and targeted at specific areas. Mahama also questioned the practicality of using a state of emergency to tackle illegal mining, which he said is affecting 10 regions across Ghana.

cards.headline: Cross-border supporters gather at Peace Arch to call for improved Canada-U.S. relations

pages.text: Canadians, Americans, and dual citizens gathered at the Peace Arch border on a Saturday to call for improved relations between Canada and the United States. The gathering occurred as Canada-U.S. trade tensions remain a central issue in the British Columbia election campaign. Participants stated the meetings are intended to build cross-border relationships and provide mutual support. According to CBC Canada, the group has met every two weeks since March 2025, amid strained relations resulting from U.S. President Donald Trump’s trade policies and 51st-state rhetoric. Janice Young, a British Columbia resident and church minister, noted the idea for the gatherings arose as tensions increased and she sought to connect with neighbors in Washington state. Peter Andrews, a resident of Ferndale, Washington, since 2003, reported attending the inaugural event last spring and has attended every subsequent meeting.

cards.headline: Landmine risks and slow clearance operations affect displaced residents in Hasakah countryside

pages.text: Villages in the countryside of Hasakah, northeastern Syria, face risks from landmines and unexploded remnants of war due to slow clearance operations and delays in the organized return of displaced families, according to residents. Displaced residents from Sere Kaniye (Ras al-Ain) told North Press that delays in organized returns are prompting individuals to return to their villages on their own. Farhan Mohammad, a displaced resident from al-Qasimiya village, stated that while three mine-clearance teams are operating in the area, the number is insufficient for the size of the territory requiring survey and clearance. Mohammad noted that most homes in the area are constructed of mud, while concrete houses have sustained extensive damage. Residents expressed a desire to return before winter to facilitate home repairs. Additionally, Mohammad reported that residents opened the road to their villages several days ago as the planting season approaches, following nearly seven years of being denied access to agricultural land. He stated that previous promises to return groups of displaced people every few days have not materialized on the ground. Mohammad added that residents of several villages are voluntarily returning almost daily due to difficult conditions in camps and schools, despite landmines remaining the primary concern for a safe return. He noted that while security conditions and landmines previously prevented returns, prolonged displacement has pushed many to return regardless of the risks. Last week, the Sere Kaniye Displaced Persons Committee called on Syrian government authorities to resume return operations and disclose obstacles hindering the return of displaced people following the suspension of organized returns.

cards.headline: Family of man killed in police-involved shooting protests for answers at Toronto police headquarters

pages.text: The family of 19-year-old Kaleym Davy protested outside Toronto police headquarters on Saturday, calling for answers regarding the circumstances of his death in August. Davy was killed during a police-involved shooting in Mississauga, near Council Ring Road and The Collegeway. His aunts, Kellise and Janelle Davy, stated the family has been left in the dark and expressed concerns regarding the use of force. Janelle Davy told CBC Toronto that the family wants to know why excessive force was used and why he was treated as a notorious gang member. 19-year-old Davy's death is currently being investigated by Ontario’s police watchdog, the Special Investigations Unit (SIU). According to SIU spokesperson Monica Hudon, the incident involved five unmarked Toronto police vehicles, three of which crashed into a Mercedes. The Toronto Police Service had been tracking the vehicle in connection with a firearms investigation. While the Mercedes had been reported stolen the day prior, the SIU stated they received updated information indicating the vehicle was not stolen. Hudon previously stated that an officer shot at least once into the vehicle and hit the driver, who was later pronounced dead at the scene.

cards.headline: Charles Amofah elected Vice President of African Bowling Federation

pages.text: Ghanaian bowling administrator Charles O. Amofah has been elected Vice President of the African Bowling Federation (BFA) following the federation’s 2026 General Assembly. According to MyJoyOnline, Amofah’s election places him in the leadership of the continental body alongside newly elected President General Ahmed Nasr of Egypt. The General Assembly also elected Ahmed Abdelhamid Gamal of Egypt as Secretary General. Amofah will serve alongside three elected board members: Sherif Abdel Moneim of Egypt, Khaled Meziou of Tunisia, and Babou Ponde of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

The General Assembly recognized the participation of Elvis Kargbo, President of the Sierra Leone Bowling Federation and a member of the General Assembly, while Mashoud Said, President of the Mauritius Bowling Federation, attended as a distinguished guest. The newly constituted BFA leadership is expected to work collectively on strengthening, developing, and promoting bowling across Africa. The federation expressed appreciation to the participating national federations, delegates, members, and guests for their contributions to the General Assembly.

cards.headline: NACOC finds no link between cocaine seizure suspects and presidential security details

pages.text: The Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) stated that background checks on suspects arrested in connection with the Dunkirk cocaine seizure found no evidence linking any individual to the security details of President John Dramani Mahama or Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang. Alexander Twum-Barimah, Deputy Director-General of NACOC, provided this clarification on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, following claims that suspect Musah Attah, also known as “Kromo,” had worked with presidential security. Twum-Barimah stated that NACOC information identifies Attah as a farmer rather than a member of the presidential security staff, noting that the commission has found nothing to prove he is with the presidency. This follows previous clarifications by NACOC that preliminary background checks had not established any suspects as presidential escorts. The controversy arose after Old Tafo Member of Parliament Vincent Ekow Assafuah claimed Attah was linked to the security details of both the President and Vice President. Addressing social media photographs purportedly showing Attah with the President and Vice President, Twum-Barimah noted that presidential security details for the President and Vice President operate in separate sections or groups and that a single officer is not assigned to both simultaneously.

cards.headline: Trump greets Xi Jinping at Joint Base Andrews as US and China extend trade truce

pages.text: On the evening of September 23, 2026, President Donald Trump and First Lady Melania Trump traveled to Joint Base Andrews in Maryland to personally greet Chinese leader Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan, upon their arrival. The greeting on the tarmac was noted as an unusual move, as US presidents typically welcome foreign leaders at the White House. The arrival ceremony included a 30-metre-long red carpet, a military flyover by two B-1 bombers, and the presentation of national anthems and flags. During the ceremony, Trump visibly winced at the sound of a US military jet flying overhead while standing with Xi during the US national anthem. This state visit occurs during the same week as the United Nations General Assembly in New York, though Xi is not scheduled to address that meeting. The two-day visit is expected to address issues including artificial intelligence development, trade, Taiwan, and climate. The White House has invited executives from companies including OpenAI, Apple, xAI, Microsoft, Nvidia, and Meta to a state dinner for Xi on Thursday. Simultaneously, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that the US and China have agreed to extend the Busan agreement, a temporary trade truce between the two economies. Bessent, who met with Chinese Vice-premier He Lifeng earlier on September 23, 2026, stated the agreement will be extended until January 10, two months past its original expiration date.

cards.headline: Patricia Appiagyei appeals to Lordina Mahama and Jane Naana over detention of Ghana Jollof accused

pages.text: Deputy Minority Leader Patricia Appiagyei has appealed to First Lady Lordina Mahama and Vice President Professor Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang to intervene in the continued detention of senior nursing officer Salomey Awiti Baffoe. The appeal follows a High Court decision on September 24, 2026, to refuse Ms. Baffoe’s application for bail in connection with the Ghana Jollof TikTok case. The court cited the cyber-related nature of the ongoing investigation and the potential risk of interference with witnesses as reasons for the refusal, subsequently directing the Republic to expedite its investigations. Ms. Baffoe faces a charge of abetting the publication of false news. The prosecution alleges she assisted Barbara Asantewaa Kodua, identified by investigators as the operator of the Ghana Jollof TikTok account, to disseminate videos and recruit others to redistribute content. Investigators have also alleged that financial transactions were uncovered between the two women.

The defense has argued for Ms. Baffoe's release, citing her constitutional presumption of innocence and her responsibilities as a mother of three. Her lawyer, Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah, stated that the continued detention is affecting the education of one of her children who is due to begin Senior High School. Speaking to JoyNews following the September 24, 2026, proceedings, Mrs. Appiagyei described the situation as troubling due to the burden placed on women responsible for the care and education of children. She characterized the situation as using women against other women and made a passionate appeal to the First Lady and Vice President, noting the impact on women and single mothers in Ghana.

cards.headline: Tigrayan rebels and new alliance launch offensive against Ethiopian government

pages.text: Fears of a return to civil war are growing in Ethiopia following an offensive by Tigrayan fighters into the neighboring states of Afar and Amhara and the formation of a new rebel alliance. On September 20, 2026, the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) announced it had formed the Ethiopian Peoples’ Forces Alliance for Survival alongside six other armed and political groups. The alliance aims to depose Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government and establish a transitional government in Ethiopia. On September 23, 2026, Tigrayan forces seized control of three airports from federal police, leading Ethiopian Airlines to suspend flights to the Tigray region. Both the federal government and Tigrayan authorities have accused the other of triggering the return to open conflict. Getachew Reda, an adviser to Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, accused Tigrayan forces of launching an all-out offensive against government positions, while Tigrayan authorities stated their forces were responding defensively to attacks by federal troops. This escalation follows months of rising tensions regarding political power, territory, and the implementation of the 2022 peace agreement. The Armed Conflict Location and Event Data organisation (ACLED) reports that Ethiopian forces have carried out drone strikes targeting TPLF officials and forces in recent months, with strikes concentrated in southern Tigray and the capital, Mekelle. A previous war between the Ethiopian army and the TPLF from 2020 to 2022 resulted in an estimated 600,000 deaths.

cards.headline: Mahama describes climate change as ultimate test of global equity at UN General Assembly

pages.text: Addressing the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York, President John Dramani Mahama described climate change as the ultimate test of global equity. He called for increased international commitment to climate justice and financing, noting that Africa contributes less than four per cent of global greenhouse gas emissions while bearing heavy burdens of climate devastation. Mahama highlighted environmental challenges including erratic rainfall, coastal erosion, and accelerating desertification in the Sahelian regions. He cited an event on 29 June this year where Ghana and coastal West Africa experienced an unprecedented deluge, stating that torrential rain exceeding 160 millimetres was dumped on seven coastal regions within 24 hours, resulting in 39 deaths and one person still missing.

Mahama stated that climate justice requires developed countries to fulfill financial commitments to nations most vulnerable to climate change impacts. He argued that climate mitigation support should be operationalized through predictable, non-debt-creating grants rather than loans that increase the debt burdens of fragile economies. The President characterized melting glaciers, flash flooding, droughts, heatwaves, brush fires, and hurricanes as unmistakable signals of an overburdened planet. Additionally, Mahama called for international solidarity regarding global health security, advocating for an equitable global health architecture that includes regional manufacturing of vaccines and therapeutics, strengthened epidemic surveillance, and financed public health infrastructure across the Global South in accordance with the Accra Reset.

cards.headline: Approximately 80 countries call for reopening of the Strait of Hormuz

pages.text: Approximately 80 countries issued a call on Thursday for the urgent reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, warning that disruptions to navigation threaten energy security and global trade. Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani read the joint statement at the United Nations, calling for the strait to be fully and urgently reopened so that vessels may transit safely and without restrictions. The statement asserted that freedom of navigation through the strait must be guaranteed without the imposition of unlawful conditions, burdens, or tolls on maritime traffic. The signatories condemned attacks by the Houthi group and Iran, which they stated threaten maritime security, international navigation, and global trade. The call for reopening follows a sharp decline in vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, a global energy route connecting the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman.

cards.headline: Iranian President says United States must choose to end war

pages.text: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stated that the United States must decide whether it wants to end the war with Iran. During an interview aired on Fox News' 'Special Report with Bret Baier' show, Pezeshkian responded to a question regarding whether the conflict could end by the end of the year by saying, 'But we do not wish to continue. It's America that must choose whether it wants to end this or not.' On September 23, 2026, Pezeshkian told the UN General Assembly that Tehran would never surrender to US pressure, noting that both sides remain far apart on how to end the war. This follows a September 22, 2026, statement from US President Donald Trump, who suggested an agreement could arrive soon but also stated he could 'annihilate' Iran if no deal is reached to end the conflict. The war began on February 28 when the US and Israel attacked Iran, prompting Tehran to respond with strikes on Israel and Gulf states hosting US bases. US-Israeli strikes on Iran and Israeli attacks on Lebanon have resulted in thousands of deaths and the displacement of millions. President Trump has identified weakening Iran's nuclear capabilities as a war objective. While the US is nuclear-armed, Iran does not possess nuclear weapons and denies seeking them, maintaining it has the right to develop nuclear technology for peaceful purposes as a party to the nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty.

cards.headline: One killed and four injured in explosion at car repair shop in Daraa countryside

pages.text: An unexplained explosion at a car repair shop in Nawa, located in western Syria’s Daraa countryside, killed one person and injured four others, including two children, on Thursday, according to the North Press Agency. A local source reported that the injured individuals were transported to Nawa National Hospital and Daraa National Hospital for medical treatment. The blast also caused damage to several nearby homes and shops, as well as the area's water and electricity networks. While repair crews and relevant authorities worked to restore services, authorities arrived at the site to begin investigating the circumstances and cause of the explosion. As of Thursday, the cause of the blast had not been determined.
